title: iOS Burst: commit the explicit disable (reproducibility) + macOS player build to re-enable (perf)
summary: M0-UNITY-01 review finding. Burst (com.unity.burst, transitive via URP / Input System / Animation Rigging) is disabled for the iOS build so the Linux game-ci export succeeds (iOS Burst AOT cannot cross-compile from Linux). Two gaps: (1) the disable is NOT committed — no ProjectSettings/BurstAotSettings_iOS.json and no CI flag — so 'Burst off' is not reproducible from a fresh checkout (SECURITY_CHECKLIST §7.1 reproducible builds); (2) Burst is a performance optimizer, so shipping with it off leaves CPU-side performance (Jobs / hot numeric loops in movement, physics, scene-graph math) on the table for device fps. Not a correctness issue and not blocking M0/M1 — the iOS splat render is GPU-sort-bound, so the M1-UNITY-01 render measurement is unaffected. Fix: make the iOS Burst state explicit + committed, and add a macOS Unity player-build lane (Burst AOT compiles arm64 natively on macOS) for perf/TestFlight builds before device perf testing.

acceptance_tests.test: The iOS Burst state is explicit and committed (ProjectSettings/BurstAotSettings_iOS.json or set in ProjectSetup.cs), so a fresh checkout reproduces the same Burst behavior; an EditMode test or a CI note records it.

A macOS Unity player-build lane produces an iOS build with Burst AOT enabled (compiles arm64 natively on macOS), used for perf/TestFlight builds; the Linux export lane stays for fast compile-check CI.
acceptance_tests.evidence: green macOS build log showing Burst enabled

acceptance_tests.test: Device fps is compared Burst-off vs Burst-on on a CPU-bound scene to quantify the gain and confirm the 30 fps target holds with Burst on. Measurements are suggested evidence (SPEC §11), not a gate.

history.event: Created by the Coordinator from the M0-UNITY-01 review (Owner flagged Burst-off + graphics=automatic). Graphics=automatic resolves to Metal-only and is correctly guarded by an EditMode test (ProjectSettingsSmokeTests) — no action needed there. Burst-off is the correct workaround for the Linux iOS export; tracked here for reproducibility + perf.

Independent secondary review (Coordinator) of the Operator's implementation (97ce8f9): BurstAotSettings_iOS.json committed ENABLED (AT-1); IosBurstBuildHook flips Burst off only for the fast Linux compile-check export (-gjIosBurstOff) and restores it; the macOS player lane builds iOS with Burst AOT on and asserts lib_burst_generated.a compiled (AT-2); EditMode tests cover committed-state + flag parsing. CI green, no secrets. Confirmed sound (exceeds the ticket spec — Burst stays ENABLED for the real/TestFlight build). AT-3 (device fps Burst-off vs on) is suggested (SPEC §11) and rides the M1 render/perf pass. Status -> done.

Operator evidence + correction to the review entry above. That review closed the ticket on 97ce8f9's Linux-lane CI; the macOS player lane had not yet produced a build: its first dispatch, ios-build 36248407406 (attempts 1 and 2), activated Unity on macOS fine (no 401s) but failed when the Package Manager's embedded Node server aborted with 'async hook stack has become corrupted' during the first package resolve. Fixed in 067b9a3 (the macOS step sets NODE_OPTIONS=--no-force-async-hooks-checks). AT-2 evidence: ios-build 36250853451 (workflow_dispatch lane=macos on main 067b9a3, macos-14 arm64) green: '[GJ-BURST] iOS Burst AOT ENABLED (committed ProjectSettings/BurstAotSettings_iOS.json; host OSXEditor)', Burst bcl.exe ran (11.9 s), 'Build Finished, Result: Success', lib_burst_generated.a arm64 739,344 bytes with 378 exported code symbols, unsigned xcodebuild BUILD SUCCEEDED (same result earlier on branch run 36249118932). Linux lane: ios-build 36250099876 (push 067b9a3) green with '[GJ-BURST] iOS Burst AOT DISABLED for this build only (-gjIosBurstOff; host LinuxEditor)' + restore; unity-tests 36250099866 EditMode 6/6 (incl. IosBurstSettingsTests) + PlayMode 1/1. AT-1 met, AT-2 met, AT-3 (device fps Burst off vs on) suggested, pending device testing. Finding: the ticket premise is outdated. On Unity 6000.0.84f1 + Burst 1.8.30, iOS Burst AOT also runs on the Linux host: the pre-M3 Linux export (ios-build 36241881048) ran bcl.exe and shipped lib_burst_generated.a, and a local Linux export with Burst on produced a 737,952-byte library. So Burst was never actually off; the Linux-lane disable is now a deliberate choice for the compile check (drop the -gjIosBurstOff customParameter to re-enable it). Status stays done.
